verdict_summary: TRUNCATION IS THE WALL. The 4096-token call returned stop_type='limit' with tokens_predicted=4096 and content_chars=12376 — the model hit the n_predict cap mid-prose. The model was generating multi-token chain-of-thought / analysis text (thinking about the WIN STATE grid) and never reached the code block before being cut off. The content tail confirms mid-sentence truncation ('The win state ...' cut off). This is not a generation-quality failure: the model is capable of writing the code, but the 4096-token budget is consumed by CoT reasoning before the code block is emitted. Raising max_tokens is the fix.

analysis.mechanism: The Qwen3.5-9B-MTP model with /no_think prefix still generates multi-step chain-of-thought analysis of the WIN STATE grid before emitting the code block. At 4096 tokens, the CoT phase exhausts the budget before the code block starts.
analysis.root_cause: max_tokens=4096 is insufficient for the L2 reinduction prompt which includes the previous_level_complete_grid WIN STATE exemplar. The model reasons about the WIN STATE (adds ~1000-2000 extra CoT tokens vs L1) before writing the code. 4096 is the L1 budget; L2 needs 6144-8192.
analysis.fix: Raise LocalGGUFProposer.max_tokens from 4096 to 8192 for L2+ reinduction calls. The comment on line 1042 ('a full world-model engine needs >2048 (it truncated mid-code)') already acknowledged this for L1 — L2 needs a higher ceiling due to the WIN STATE CoT overhead.
analysis.secondary_observation: The /no_think prefix does NOT suppress CoT on the L2 reinduction prompt — the model ignores it when faced with a complex WIN STATE puzzle. This may require a stronger prompt instruction ('Do not analyze, output code directly.').
